correctness.rationale: The strict improvement event under a fully candidate-exchangeable ballot is contained in the unique-maximum event among floor(k/t)+1 disjoint equal-size blocks, hence has probability <=b_{k,t}. Integer arithmetic gives minimal gap 1/[k(k+1)] at t=1. Total variation controls average event probability for heterogeneous voters, and Jensen plus Chernoff yields the claimed finite n bound; the all-committees statement is a finite union bound. A biased one-approval law on m=k+1 ballots reaches the equality threshold, with binomial CLT limiting failure 1/2 for k>=2 (certain failure k=1); above it failure tends to one. The unbiased binomial large deviation sandwich yields D(1/k || 1/(k+1)). Independently checked all exchangeable fixed-cardinality ballot orbits for 2<=m<=6, every k,W,T; no violation. These checks do not establish voter-correlated concentration; independence across voters is required.
